newsitem.title: USA: Most IMM currencies end down after weak session.
newsitem.headline: Most IMM currencies end down after weak session.

text.p: Most IMM currency futures finished lower, never completely recovering from overnight losses and U.S. data.
The dollar's decisive rally above 120.00 yen and 1.56 marks overnight set a bearish tone across the board in currencies, and tame fourth-quarter U.S. Employment Cost Index secured the early dim tone.
Treasury bond futures soared more than a point on those data, and stocks posted huge morning gains. ECI rose 0.8 percent, compared with a forecast for up 0.9 and a third-quarter gain of 0.6 percent.
In afteroon trade, March marks, Swiss, and sterling staged a slight recovery to end still lower but off the day's lows.
"It wasn't very convincing as anything other than profittaking," an IMM trader said.
March yen was under seige by bearish sentiments all session, setting several new contract lows and trading at the lowest price for a lead contract since early 1993.

"The move is starting to accelerate," said Peter McTeague, technical market strategist for MCM TradeWatch. "There's nothing to say that a low has been scored in yen, and the dialogue is good for the dollar," he said.
He pegged a dollar/yen upside target of 124 to 125 yen.
Technical yen weakness amid the overnight dollar rally was exacerbated by comments reported from a Ministry of Finance (MOF) official that the MOF was not worried by the yen's depreciation.
The dollar stalled at a 47-month high against the yen near midday, then retreated on rumors the Federal Reserve had checked rates for the Bank of Japan (BOJ).
"It's all speculation and nothing is confirmed," the floor trader said.
"But the fact that they (the BOJ) have not come in for any notable size at all to defend their yen really says a lot, like (targets at) 123 and 125," the floor trader said.

March marks posted a contract low overnight at $0.6053 but managed to stay above that low in day session trading. Traders tied overnight dollar/mark strength to comments from Juergen Stark, state secretary at the German Finance Ministry. He said dollar strength was a "normalisation" of an overvalued mark.
Day session dollar strength was tied to sharp gains in Treasury bonds and U.S. stocks, traders said.
In morning trade, U.S. January consumer confidence was reported at 116.8 versus a revised 114.2 in December.

At the close, March yen was down $0.000120 to $0.008307, marks fell $0.0009 to $0.6087, Swiss francs lost $0.0008 to $0.7029, sterling eased $0.0066 to $1.6164, Canadian dollar rose $0.0019 to $0.7483, Aussie dollar fell $0.0041 to $0.7685, Mexican peso rose $0.000375 to $0.124825.
